programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.sub-title: Puebla, Where the Good Cooks Are From

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.sub-title: Singapore: New York in Twenty Years
programme.desc: Tony sets out to find the real Singapore, with its multicultural restaurants and food markets. He samples prescription food dishes, explores the Geyland Serai Market, and rides the clean and efficient local subway.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: London, England: In London, Tony attempts to dispel the myth that all English food is disgusting and over-boiled. Tony tries Nose to Tail Eating, explores traditional fare at Pie and Mash Shoppes, and then visits a predominantly Indian community.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.sub-title: Down Under: The Wild West of Cooking
programme.desc: Melbourne, Australia boasts hard-living, good-natured, and eccentric lovers of food - Tony's kind of people. In search of the outlaws of food, Tony explores a pasteurization-free cheese factory, and an old-world cured jamon workshop.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: What is a Carioca? The natives of Rio de Janiero, Brazil are lovable scamps who find ways to avoid work, preferring the beach, flirting, and hanging out at restaurants and bars instead. Tony, under the tutelage of an exemplary Carioca, gives the lifestyle a try.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: Join Tony on his quest to characterize the perfect bar in New York City. Discover the importance of a maniacal bartender, the proper chemical makeup of drinks, the joys of seedy dive-bars, and the need for late-night snacks.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: Known as Brazil's capital of happiness, Salvador da Bahia offers fruitful local markets, and rich Bahian cuisine. Here, Tony takes part in a traditional local ceremony, and experiences the culinary talents of the famous Bahian artist of the kitchen - Chef Dada.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.sub-title: Cobra Heart-Food That Makes You Manly
programme.desc: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: After taking a cyclo-ride through Ho Chi Minh City and trying various foods from roadside vendors and markets, Tony tests his might with a few shots of snake wine and a live cobra heart.

programme.sub-title: Down Under: The Wild West of Cooking
programme.desc: Melbourne, Australia boasts hard-living, good-natured, and eccentric lovers of food - Tony's kind of people. In search of the outlaws of food, Tony explores a pasteurization-free cheese factory, and an old-world cured jamon workshop.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: Jumping into a Thai tuk tuk taxi, Tony attempts to soak up Thai culture, and get lost in the cuisine of Chiang Mai, Thailand.

programme.title: Anthony Bourdain A Cook's Tour
programme.desc: Oaxaca, Mexico: Chef Tony Bourdain explores the exotic and colorful indigenous zone of Mexico's Oaxaca region where he tastes toasted grasshoppers and other delicacies. His adventure ends with mariachi music and, of course, lots of tequila.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: At the AYANA Resort and Spa in Bali, Dava Steak and Seafood Restaurant serves up modern French-Asian cuisine created by award-winning Singaporean chef Jusman So. Taste a few of Dava's savory dishes and visit AYANA Resort's famous Rock Bar.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: The Tippling Club pairs award-winning cuisine with world-class cocktails and pushes the limits of combining fresh ingredients with unique textures. Chef and Owner Ryan Clift's inspiring culinary journey shines through in Tippling's dishes.

programme.title: The Toque 12
programme.desc: Meet the genius behind Chef Nancy Silverton and witness her make one of her celebrated pizzas from scratch. Mario Batali provides sage advice for young chefs, and Wolfgang Puck and Greg Bess take you into their culinary world at Spago.

programme.title: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.sub-title: Off the Beaten Path in Huatulco
programme.desc: Mexico's beaches glimmer with pristine perfection. Chef Rick Bayless takes us off the beaten path to find great food and even better beaches such as Playa Chahue and Playa Principal. You would be well-advised to follow his lead.

programme.title: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: The Mercado Lazaro Cardenas is standard as far as markets in Mexico City go, but turn one corner, and you are in the world of coffee geeks, of which Rick is a proud citizen. Rick also meets with mixologists Joseph Mortera and Ricardo Nava.

programme.title: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: To beat the heat, Rick leaves the kitchen for a cookout a la Mexicana, inspired by one of his world-favorite meat eateries: El Canelo, near Guadalajara. Rick also provides a quick lesson in setting up a home grill for wood-fired cooking.

programme.title: Rituals of the World
programme.sub-title: Ethiopia: A Baptism in the Sky
programme.desc: Journey to the Tigray region of Ethiopia, Africa where Orthodox Christians confront their fears and baptize their children in churches perched 800 meters in the sky in the troglodyte church of Abuna Yemata Guh. The climb is excruciatingly difficult, and extremely dangerous.

programme.title: Rituals of the World
programme.desc: Each May, the Quechuas of the high plateau converge on Macha a spectacular and violent ritual called Tinku, a fertility ritual in the form of fighting. The blood that is shed feeds Pachamama, the Earth Mother, who is responsible for good harvests, fertility in women, and a large herd of llamas.

programme.title: Rituals of the World
programme.desc: Every year in Jacmel, on the southern coast of Haiti, festivities take on an intensity not found elsewhere. Haitians do not depict dream-like characters in their parades, but instead, monsters or specters. This is a way for them to deal with the difficulties of the past, and those of the present.

programme.title: Secrets of the National Parks
programme.sub-title: The Secrets of Glacier National Park
programme.desc: Experience high adventure in "the land of shining mountains." Take an unforgettable hike along the Highline Trail, raft a wild river, and travel by train aboard the renowned Empire Builder. Behold massive glaciers and get close (but not too close!) to bears. Then, relax at a high-altitude chalet.

programme.title: Green Paradise
programme.desc: In the middle of the vast Pacific Ocean, the resplendent Tuamotus Archipelago is a large group of islands and atolls in French Polynesia. Displaying stunning tropical beauty, the island's local population faces the challenge of preserving the entire ecosystem of precious coral gardens offshore.

programme.title: Green Paradise
programme.desc: Isolated from geopolitics for the past 30 years, Laos is now slowly opening to tourism. Its cultures and environment are fragile, and a responsible form of tourism could preserve its past and character. From fishing villages to the forests of northern Laos, meet the people that protect their land.

programme.title: Lonely Planet: Best Parks Ever - America's National Parks
programme.sub-title: Best Parks for a Deep Freeze
programme.desc: National parks cover all kinds of terrain, including the frozen kind. Take a look at why these snowy conditions are worth all the chills.

programme.title: Bare Feet with Mickela Mallozzi
programme.desc: Mickela celebrates black voices in the arts by dancing with the renowned Dance Theatre of Harlem and the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater. She also drums and dances with the Brooklyn United Marching Band and pays homage to Juneteenth.

programme.title: Bare Feet with Mickela Mallozzi
programme.desc: Mickela learns the Kandyan dance at the Sri Lankan Dance Academy and visits the family-owned restaurants on Victory Blvd. that prepare traditional dishes. She also celebrates with the incredibly diverse community through song and cricket.

programme.title: Laura McKenzie's Traveler
programme.desc: Join Laura and feast on famous Roman fare, witness timeless architecture, and admire the endless artwork Rome offers. Also, visit Piazza Navona where you can shop until you drop. Then it is off to the Frascati Valley, home to Casal Pilozzo.

programme.title: Laura McKenzie's Traveler
programme.desc: Enter 12 miles of enclosing walls, 26 acres of roof, and over 2,000 windows and experience the royal Palace of Versailles. If you are looking for some good ole' fun, then you will enjoy Parc Asterix. Place Vendome is the top spot for high-end merchandise.

programme.title: Laura McKenzie's Traveler
programme.desc: Auckland is New Zealand's largest city. Laura takes an hour's drive south of Auckland to a working sheep farm in the New Zealand countryside. A few miles down the road, Laura spies a familiar sight - Hobbiton, the set from the Lord of the Rings films where Bilbo lived before and after his journey.

programme.title: Porthole Cruise and Travel Show
programme.sub-title: Enchanted Princess: New Gland and Canada
programme.desc: The next time you think about cruising New England and Canada your best bet is aboard the Enchanted Princess, a medallion-class ship with stops in Boston, Bar Harbor, New Brunswick, and Nova Scotia. Bill will show you all the hot spots.

programme.title: Jeremy Pang's Asian Kitchen
programme.desc: Jeremy's BBQ Chicken Wings with Spicy Slaw is sure to impress. Joe prepares a perfect Malaysian Fried Rice. After being inspired by Drunken Prawns in a home dedicated to whisky, Jeremy makes Cinnamon Bao Doughnuts and Chocolate Sauce.

programme.title: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: Who do Mexico City's top chefs believe will be the next great chef to emerge from Mexico? Pablo Salas. The odd thing is, Salas does not work in Mexico City. His restaurant, Amaranta, is in Toluca, and Rick travels to meet him there.

programme.title: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programme.desc: The corn tortilla is the canvas upon which Mexico creates some of its most classic cuisine. Rick shows us three styles of tortilla in Mexico City: steak tacos al carbon, bistec tacos a la plancha, and stewed tacos de guisado.

programme.title: Ottolenghi's Mediterranean Island Feast
programme.desc: Beginning in the exquisite fishing port of Bosa, Yotam prepares one of the Mediterranean's classic meals: freshly caught lobster on an open fire pit. Leaving the coast behind, he then travels into the rugged Sardinian heartland.

programme.title: Mythical Roads
programme.desc: Located on the Baltic Sea, the countries of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania share a common destiny but possess different identities. Trek along the 1,000 km road through these countries that begins in the North of Poland, in the Kashubia region near Gdansk, and meet warm and caring people.

programme.title: Mythical Roads
programme.desc: From the Kalahari gates to Epupa Falls, through the Namibian and Skeleton Coasts, cross the most spectacular deserts and oases of Africa. Along the way, meet people with a thousand faces and lifestyles. By their side, he discovers this "wisdom of water," which is the real wealth of Namibia.

programme.title: Lonely Planet: Best Parks Ever - America's National Parks
programme.sub-title: Best Parks for Jaw Dropping Scenery
programme.desc: See Mother Nature at its best. From the highest waterfall to the one of the biggest holes in the world, it's this kind of scenery that will make you stop in your tracks.

programme.title: Bare Feet with Mickela Mallozzi
programme.desc: Mickela attends Le Fete de Bayonne to celebrate French Basque Country tradition. This includes dancing the Fandango, handling giant puppets, tasting the region's traditional cuisine, and experiencing the renowned Pastorale.

programme.title: Bare Feet with Mickela Mallozzi
programme.desc: Mickela gets transported to Haiti in the streets of Flatbush, Brooklyn through Haitian drum lessons and dance classes, and by visiting local shops dedicated to uplifting Haitian culture.

programme.title: Moments in Time with Elia Locardi
programme.desc: Elia accidentally discovers the perfect spot for a sunrise shot of Kuala Lumpur, then meets-up with Grey Chow, a longtime friend and native. They venture outside the city to explore the Batu Caves, one of Malaysia's biggest attractions.

programme.title: Moments in Time with Elia Locardi
programme.desc: Elia shares advice on traveling with camera equipment and navigating Tokyo's subway system. He visits a peaceful garden then heads to the crowded Shibuya Crossing. Lastly, he visits the Photo History Museum and speaks with Sam Minami.

programme.title: Moments in Time with Elia Locardi
programme.desc: Elia explores the Odaiba waterfront with Giovanni Piliarvu, photographing the Rainbow Bridge. Then meets with Fujifilm's team to discuss the ever-changing market of photography. He ends with a memorable visit to the Robot Restaurant.

programme.title: Tastes Like Home
programme.desc: After learning the secret behind Nikki's savory recipe for pork stuffed with prunes, Catherine travels from Wicklow to Gran Canaria where she prepares the much-adored dish for Nikki's sister, Jill, and explores the rugged Canary Islands.
